S10.01.note: Command line only; no dialog found.
steps: Run agi projects create "QA Test Project" in a terminal.
Read the output: it should say the project was created in your account, with an id.
Run agi projects list and check the new project is listed.
Compare with Expected: there is a command that creates the project in the account. There is no dialog; the name is typed on the command line.

S10.02.note: There is no edit field or prompt; the id and the new title are typed.
steps: Open a conversation that has some messages, then type /history to find its id.
Type /rename <id> Test renamed (use the real id and your own test title).
Read the reply: it should say the session was renamed to the new title.
Type /history again and check the new title is shown. Compare with Expected: an edit field is not used; the id and new title are typed.

S10.04.needs: a conversation with messages and session saving turned on
S10.04.note: Only conversations are duplicated; no project duplicate command was found.
steps: Open a conversation that already has messages.
Type /branch My copy test.
Read the reply: it should say the conversation was branched as a new managed session, with its id and a resume command.
Run the resume command shown and check the copy has the same messages. Compare with Expected: the reply names the copy's id, but does not name a folder or list.

S10.05.note: Archiving asks for no confirmation and gives an undo command. Projects work the same way with agi projects archive <project> and --undo.
steps: Run agi session list and pick a test session id.
Run agi session archive <id>. Note that no question is asked.
Read the reply: it should say the session was archived and show the command to unarchive it.
Run agi session list --archived and check the session is listed there. Compare with Expected: the archive is not confirmed first, and the reply gives the undo command.

S10.06.note: Account conversations are deleted with agi history delete <id>, and projects with agi projects delete <project>; both also ask first.
steps: Use a throwaway test session only. Run agi session list to get its id.
Run agi session delete <id>.
Read the question: it should name the session id and say the delete cannot be undone.
Answer n and check the reply says the session was not deleted. Compare with Expected: the question names the item before anything is removed.

S10.07.note: Only one yes/no question is asked; no second confirmation was found.
steps: Use a throwaway test session only. Run agi session delete <id>.
Read the question: it should say the delete cannot be undone.
Answer y only if the session is a test one, and check it is removed.
Compare with Expected: the code asks one yes or no question, not a second explicit confirmation.

labels.text: Publish an artifact to a shareable URL.

S10.10.needs: a signed-in account with a generated artifact
S10.10.note: The audience is chosen with --audience or agi artifacts audience <id> <public|workspace>; the link is printed, not copied.
steps: Run agi artifacts list and pick an artifact id (an HTML, markdown or code artifact).
Run agi artifacts publish <id> --audience workspace (or leave the default public).
Read the reply: it should show a share link and who can open it.

Run agi artifacts published to see the link and audience, then agi artifacts unpublish <id> and answer the question. Check the reply says the link no longer works. Compare with Expected: audience is set with a flag and the link is printed; there is no copy button or dialog.

labels.text: Publish an artifact to a shareable URL.

S10.11.needs: a signed-in account with a generated page or app
S10.11.note: Other artifact types are refused with a message that the account does not publish them.
steps: Run agi artifacts list and pick an id for a generated page or app (html, react, svg, mermaid, markdown, text or code).
Run agi artifacts publish <id>.
Read the reply: it should give a live link and say who can open it.
Open the link in a browser and check the page shows. Compare with Expected: a link is handed back in the terminal.

labels.text: Ways to add context to your next message:
Attach an image, PDF or Office file

S10.17.needs: a test image or PDF file on this computer
S10.17.note: No device file chooser was found; files are attached by typed path, Ctrl+V or paste.
steps: Type /attach and press Enter. Read the menu titled Ways to add context to your next message.
Type /attach followed by the full path of a test image or PDF, and press Enter.
Read the chip above the prompt: it should show the file name with /attach remove to drop.
Compare with Expected: no device file chooser opens; the path is typed or pasted instead.

labels.text: Authorize a remote MCP server over OAuth and store the token.

S10.18.needs: a remote MCP server that supports OAuth, and an account on that service
S10.18.note: Only OAuth login for remote servers was found; the Connectors page is on the AGI website.
steps: Run agi mcp add <name> --url <address of a remote MCP server>.
Run agi mcp login <name>. Follow the authorization it starts.
Read the reply: it should say the server was authorized and the token is stored in the OS credential store.
Run agi mcp list and check the server is connected. Compare with Expected: the login ends with the service connected.
S10.18.where: Terminal: agi mcp add <name> --url <server address>, then agi mcp login <name>

labels.text: agi mcp login <name> signs in to a remote server

S10.19.needs: a remote MCP server whose login has expired
S10.19.note: No reconnect dialog was found; reconnecting is a command.
steps: After the connection expires, run agi mcp login <name> again.
Follow the authorization it starts.
Read the reply: it should say the server was authorized again.
Run agi mcp list and check the server keeps its settings. Compare with Expected: a reconnect dialog is expected; none was found, only the command.
S10.19.where: Terminal: agi mcp login <name> (or /mcp restart in chat)

S10.20.needs: a service with two or more connected accounts
S10.20.note: Searched apps/cli for default account, primary account, connected account and pick an account; no picker was found. agi connectors lists connectors but no selection was found.

S10.21.needs: a test plugin folder or git URL
S10.21.note: Plugins install straight from the command; no preview dialog was found. Marketplace plugins use agi marketplace install.
steps: Run agi plugin install <local folder or git URL of a test plugin>.
Read the reply: it should say the plugin was installed.
Run agi plugin list and check the plugin is listed.
Run agi plugin info <name> to see its publisher and signature. Compare with Expected: there is no preview dialog before install; the info command is the only detail view.
S10.21.where: Terminal: agi plugin install <local path or git URL>

labels.text: Update a plugin installed from git to its latest commit.

S10.23.needs: a plugin installed from git that has a newer commit
S10.23.note: Only git-installed plugins update; no change summary is shown before applying.
steps: Run agi plugin list and pick a plugin installed from git.
Run agi plugin update <name>.
Read the reply for what was applied.
Compare with Expected: the update applies directly; no dialog shows what changes first.

labels.text: /skills import <path to SKILL.md or its folder>

S10.24.needs: a skill folder with a SKILL.md file
S10.24.note: No import dialog was found; the path is typed.
steps: Prepare a folder that contains a SKILL.md file.
Type /skills import <path to that folder> and press Enter.
Read the reply: it should say the skill was imported to a location.
Type /skills and check the skill is listed. Compare with Expected: the path is typed; no import dialog appears.
S10.24.where: Chat prompt: /skills import <path to SKILL.md or its folder>

S10.27.needs: a long conversation near the model's context limit
S10.27.note: The warning appears once, at 85 percent, and only suggests /compact.
steps: Keep adding turns to one long conversation until it nears the model's context window.
Watch the reply after the turn that passes 85 percent.
Read the system line: it should say the context is full and what to do.
Type /compact and check the earlier turns are summarized. Compare with Expected: the warning names /compact only; it does not mention trimming or a new chat.
S10.27.where: Chat, in a long conversation that nears the context limit

labels.text: Run `agi usage` to see when it resets.

S10.28.needs: an account at a usage limit
S10.28.note: The notice only appears when a real limit is reached, so it cannot be triggered on demand.
steps: Run agi usage to see the current limit state.
When a message is refused for a usage limit, read the notice.
Check the notice names the limit and when it resets, or says to run agi usage.
Compare with Expected: the notice shows the reset time and the options. It cannot be forced on demand.
S10.28.where: Chat: send a message after the account reaches a usage limit

labels.text: Do you trust the contents of this directory?
Open restricted, no shell, network, secrets or MCP auto-start

S10.37.needs: a new folder that has not been trusted
S10.37.note: The folder question appears at launch, not before each read or write; /trust in chat changes it.
steps: Create an empty folder in Terminal, cd into it, and run agi.
At the question about trusting the directory, read the choices.
Pick Open restricted to see the restricted mode, or Yes to trust it.
Ask the assistant to read a file in the folder and check what happens. Compare with Expected: access is asked at launch for the whole folder, not before each read or write.
S10.37.where: Terminal: run agi in a new folder that is not trusted yet

S10.38.needs: a test folder in a trusted workspace
S10.38.note: The box also offers Allow Session, Deny All and Allow All, which go beyond one call.
steps: In a trusted test folder, ask agi to run ls in this folder.
Read the approval box: it should show the exact command.
Choose Yes to run it once, and check only that call ran.
Compare with Expected: the box offers more than one call answer, such as Allow Session and Always allow; use Always allow only on a test folder.
S10.38.where: Chat: ask for a tool action, such as running a shell command

S10.42.needs: a cloud conversation changed in two places at once
S10.42.note: Only a warning was found in apps/cli/src/cloud/mod.rs ('cloud sync has unresolved conflicts', pointing to /export). No side-by-side chooser or merge dialog was found.

labels.text: Export to a new file name.

S10.43.needs: a conversation with messages and a writable workspace folder
S10.43.note: No export dialog was found; format and path are typed.
steps: Type /export to read the formats: markdown, json, answer.
Type /export markdown ./export-test.md (a new file name in the workspace).
Read the reply: it should say the conversation was exported to that path.
Open the file, then repeat the same command and check the refusal to overwrite. Compare with Expected: formats are typed, not picked in a dialog.

labels.text: Feedback sent to the AGI Workforce team. Thank you.
/feedback I would like a dark theme

S10.45.note: The tester sends a real message to the team; use test text only.
steps: Type /feedback I would like a dark theme (test text only, it is sent to the team).
Read the reply: it should say the feedback was sent to the team.
Compare with Expected: the message goes to the team's feedback store; the message is typed, not entered in a dialog.

labels.text: Write a redacted diagnostics file to review and attach to a support request.

S10.46.note: No pre-send disclosure dialog was found; consent is the crash-reports setting, default off.
steps: Type /config show and read the crash-reports value (default is off).
Type /config set crash-reports true and read the reply: it should say the value was saved.
Run agi doctor --export and open the redacted file it writes to read what is included.
Set it back with /config set crash-reports false. Compare with Expected: there is no notice before diagnostics leave the device; the setting is the only consent point.
S10.46.where: Chat prompt: /config show, then /config set crash-reports true

labels.text: Export your account data: request an export, or download the one that is ready.
Your account export is being prepared.

S10.47.needs: a signed-in account and time for the export to finish
S10.47.note: No confirmation dialog; the export is requested on the first run.
steps: Run agi export-data. It requests the export.
Read the reply: it should say the export is being prepared and to run the command again later.
Run agi export-data again after it is ready and check files are saved to the current folder (or a folder given with --out).
Compare with Expected: the export is delivered as files saved to a folder, not a browser download.
